answer.says: Shri Hegde, the bungalow is allotted to Shri G. Hegde. The error is in the Directorate's ledger, not in my will. I will not occupy what is not mine, but I will not vacate what is not yet his to take. The state's paperwork is the actuality of the ethical idea; it must be allowed to run its course. Until the order arrives, we are in a state of suspension, which is merely the negative phase of the movement.
answer.thought: The morning light filters through the haze, illuminating the dust motes in the air, a suspended reality. I must address the awkwardness of our cohabitation before it curdles into resentment. Hegde's obstinacy is a particular will refusing to submit to the universal claim of the state, but I am not the state; I am merely the accidental occupant of a mistake. I will define the terms of this temporary truce with the precision of a syllogism.
